Respective

/rih-SPEK-tiv/ — stress on SPEK · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Respective describes something that belongs individually to each particular person or thing in a group, rather than being shared.

After the field trip, the buses dropped the students back at their respective schools.

Worked Example

The two rival companies presented their respective annual reports to investors.

Respect + -ive, but with a meaning-drift: not 'showing respect' (that's respectful) but 'each in its own place.' The Latin root respicere means 'to look back at.' The sentence shows respective's actual meaning: each company has its own individual report, separate from the other.

How Respective Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

individual

individual: belonging to one particular person alone

particular

particular: specific to a certain single one

separate

separate: distinct and apart from the others

Antonyms

shared

shared: belonging to everyone in common

collective

collective: owned or done by the whole group

How Strong Is It? — general → separate → individual → respective

general vs. respective

general vs. respective: 'General' covers everyone loosely at once, while respective points each person to their own specific spot.

separate vs. respective

separate vs. respective: 'Separate' only says things are apart; respective goes further, tying each item to its own particular owner.

individual vs. respective

individual vs. respective: 'Individual' highlights one person at a time, but respective is the most precise, matching every member of a group to their own thing.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — respect

Root — respect: regard, consideration — from Latin respicere, 'to look back at' (Latin)

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: having the quality or tendency of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Respect + -ive literally builds 'having the quality of regard,' but the meaning drifted: respective does not mean 'showing respect' (that word is respectful) — it means each thing considered in relation to its own owner, 'individually one's own.'

Use the root in a new word: respectively

Word Choice

neutral

Use respective when assigning or referring to multiple people's or things' individual belongings or roles—especially in formal, structured contexts like team assignments, legal settlements, or organizational roles. The word emphasizes that each person/thing has their own, distinct from others.
